description: Despite targeted sq queries using the correct local term 'konsultim publik' plus 'projekt-rregullore'/'draft rregullore' scoped to bqk-kos.org, no dedicated BQK page or index listing draft regulations currently open for public consultation was located in this pass.

result.result_summary: Only in-document evidence of consultation was found (the Climate & Environmental Risk Strategic Roadmap PDF records a May 2020 public-consultation release). No standing 'Konsultimet publike' section on bqk-kos.org surfaced in search.

why_it_matters: Consultations are an explicit topic of this cell and the earliest possible signal of a rule change. If BQK exposes drafts only via ad-hoc news posts or direct emails to licensed banks, the collection strategy must shift to the news feed + document-internal markers rather than a consultation index.

description: Every attempted WebFetch against bqk-kos.org and env2.bqk-kos.org returned HTTP 403 Forbidden, so no page HTML could be read directly in this pass; all structural knowledge here is derived from search-engine indexing of those same pages.

result.result_summary: 2/2 fetch attempts 403. Pages are clearly live (freshly indexed, including June 2026 board-decision posts).

why_it_matters: This is a bot-defence hypothesis, not a dead site. The downstream collector must use a JS-capable headless browser with a realistic user agent; a naive requests-based crawler will report the entire primary source as unreachable.

description: konsultimet.rks-gov.net was confirmed to exist and to be the statutory consultation platform, but no BQK-issued draft regulation was found on it in this pass; the only BQK-adjacent instrument surfaced was a joint MF-BQK regulation (Nr. 01/2014) on government securities markets.

result.result_summary: Platform confirmed; BQK presence on it unconfirmed.

why_it_matters: BQK is an independent institution and may be outside the scope of the government consultation platform (which is run by the OPM Office for Good Governance for ministries and government agencies). If so, the portal is a low-yield channel for this cell and effort should concentrate on BQK's own news stream.

description: No RSS/Atom feed or open data API for BQK regulations or board decisions was confirmed. The site is WordPress-based (wp-content/uploads paths, permalink slugs), which makes /feed/ endpoints plausible, but this was not verified.

result.result_summary: Structural inference only; feed URLs are a hypothesis to test, not a found source.

why_it_matters: A working WordPress feed would turn the highest-value stream (news + board decisions) from a scraping problem into a cheap polling problem.

description: A targeted query for the Kosovo Banking Association (Shoqata e Bankave të Kosovës) at the guessed domain bankassoc-kos.com returned no results from that domain at all; the association's live domain and whether it publishes industry comment letters on BQK drafts remain unestablished.

result.result_summary: Zero hits from the hypothesised domain; only BQK documents returned.

why_it_matters: The banking association is the natural venue for industry pushback on draft regulations — a strong indirect signal of contested provisions and deadline extensions. Its absence is a real gap in the indirect layer of this cell.

description: Law 08/L-304 on Banks could not be located on gzk.rks-gov.net by search, even though BQK hosts both sq and sr texts and the sr version's header cites Official Gazette No. 2 of 27 January 2026.

result.result_summary: Gazette record not surfaced by search; BQK-hosted PDFs are currently the accessible route to the text.

why_it_matters: Search-engine coverage of GZK appears to lag recent acts. Any pipeline that treats GZK search as the discovery mechanism will miss the newest and most consequential instruments; ActID enumeration or the gazette's own browse-by-date is needed.

description: WebFetch of https://bqk-kos.org/sistemet-e-pagesave/?lang=en returned HTTP 403 Forbidden. Other bqk-kos.org URLs are indexed by search engines and PDFs under /wp-content/uploads/ and /repository/docs/ resolve in search results.

result.result_summary: HYPOTHESIS: the CBK site is behind a WAF/bot filter that rejects non-browser user agents on HTML pages. Not evidence the site is dead. Collection will need a headless browser or realistic headers.

why_it_matters: The single most important source for this cell is the CBK site; an automated collector using naive HTTP will silently return zero content and be misread as 'no new regulation'.

description: Searched in Albanian for a CBK public-consultation channel for draft regulations ('projektrregullore', 'konsultim publik') and found no dedicated CBK consultation page in results; only the government-wide pre-legislative concept-document route and OPM/Assembly channels surfaced.

result.result_summary: No confirmed CBK-specific draft-regulation consultation portal. Draft regulations may be circulated to the industry (e.g. via the Banking Association) rather than published.

why_it_matters: Consultations are an explicit topic in scope; if CBK does not publish drafts, the earliest observable signal is the Board approval press release, which shortens lead time on regulatory change to near zero.

description: Albanian and English searches for a Kosovo instant-payments regulation ('rregullore për pagesat e menjëhershme', 'instant payments regulation CBK') returned only a May 2026 CBK/KBA workshop and strategy-level statements, not a binding regulation or a mandated go-live date.

result.result_summary: As of this run, instant payments in Kosovo appear to be at infrastructure/strategy stage; no dated regulatory mandate located.

why_it_matters: Instant-payment mandates are the cell's highest-value deadline signal; its absence should be recorded as 'not yet issued', not assumed missing from the search.

description: Serbian-language search ('Centralna banka Kosova propisi platni promet elektronski novac licenciranje') was dominated by Serbia/Montenegro central-bank content and dinar-related political coverage rather than CBK payments rulemaking.

result.result_summary: Serbian terminology is noisy for this cell: 'platni promet', 'uredba', 'CBK' collide with NBS/CBCG sources and with the dinar dispute. Only one CBK Serbian regulation PDF surfaced directly.

why_it_matters: Serbian coverage must be obtained by enumerating the CBK site's own 'SRB-' prefixed files and ?lang=sr variants rather than by open-web Serbian search.

description: No standalone public KIPS rulebook / participation agreement document was located; only the CBK web description of the four-phase accession process and the separate regulation on non-bank PSP access.

result.result_summary: The operational KIPS rulebook may be issued to participants rather than published on the open web.

why_it_matters: Interbank clearing rules and cut-off/session changes would then be invisible to open-source collection and must be inferred from CBK web pages, annual reports, or industry sources.

description: Albanian-language queries aimed at law-firm alerts ('njoftim ligjor', 'buletin ligjor', 'ndryshimet në ligjin bankar', 'analizë avokat') returned almost exclusively primary sources (Gazeta Zyrtare, BQK PDFs, ATK presentations, Kuvendi) and NGO/think-tank analyses (GAP Institute, KCSF, IKD), not law-firm client alerts.

result.result_summary: No Kosovo law firm was found publishing a dated banking/payments legal alert in Albanian; the firms that do publish (RPHS, Vokshi & Lata) do so in English.

why_it_matters: It means the 'summarised before an English version exists' assumption of this cell is inverted for Kosovo: the firm layer is English-first, and the Albanian-first layer is regulators plus NGOs. Local-language monitoring for this cell should target regulator and NGO outputs, not firm newsletters.

description: No Serbian-language (sr) professional-interpreter source for Kosovo banking/payments regulation was located in this run; searches were executed in sq and en, and Serbian-language legal-advisory content addressing Kosovo (XK) regulation did not surface via the queries used.

result.result_summary: Zero sr-language law-firm or advisory alert sources identified for this cell.

why_it_matters: Serbian-language coverage of Kosovo financial regulation is a stated run requirement; leaving it empty risks missing the northern-Kosovo/Serbia-facing advisory layer, which may interpret CBK rules differently.

description: For KPMG and EY, only office/overview pages were confirmed; the specific Kosovo tax & legal alert index URL was not observed. Deloitte's Kosovo alerts sit on the Albania (www2.deloitte.com/al) hub which is mid-migration to deloitte.com/ce, so the listing URL may redirect.

result.result_summary: PwC Kosovo has an explicit Tax News page; Deloitte has a confirmed Albania/Kosova alert index (possibly moving); KPMG and EY Kosovo alert indexes remain unlocated.

why_it_matters: Without stable index URLs the crawler cannot reliably detect new alerts; a manual triage pass is needed before scheduling collection.

description: Beyond a single Lexology item on Draft Law 08/L-295 on Crypto-Assets, no systematic law-firm channel commenting on CBK/Ministry public consultations was found.

result.result_summary: Firm commentary in Kosovo clusters after adoption ('law enters into force'), not during consultation.

why_it_matters: The 'consultations' topic in this run is poorly served by the professional-interpreter cell; consultation monitoring must lean on CBK/Kuvendi primary channels (other cells).

description: Searched in Albanian for a Klan Kosova and a Kosovapress business/economy desk covering BQK regulation. Neither outlet returned a banking-regulation article or an identifiable economy-section URL in any of the searches run.

result.result_summary: Klan Kosova surfaced only via its Wikipedia entry; Kosovapress returned no on-topic hits at all. No usable section URL recorded for either — deliberately not invented.

why_it_matters: Two of the outlets named in the cell definition are unconfirmed as regulatory-news sources; the cell's coverage therefore leans on Koha, Telegrafi, Ekonomia Online, Kallxo and Insajderi instead.

description: Explicit search for RSS/feed endpoints for the Albanian-language Kosovo outlets (Telegrafi, Zëri, Bota Sot, Ekonomia Online, Indeksonline) returned no feed URLs.

result.result_summary: No RSS URL was found for any Kosovo Albanian outlet in this pass; conventional WordPress /feed/ paths are a hypothesis only and were not tested.

why_it_matters: Collection will likely have to rely on HTML section crawling rather than feeds, which is more brittle and more likely to trip bot defences.

description: No consistent Albanian term for a formal regulator public-consultation process surfaced in media coverage. 'Konsultim publik' and 'projektrregullore' returned government/agriculture and PDF regulation texts, not BQK consultation announcements reported by media.

result.result_summary: Media appear not to report BQK consultations as consultations; they report the finished rule or the cabinet approval of a draft law.

why_it_matters: Confirms the cell rationale in reverse: consultations that 'open quietly' may not surface in media at all, so the media layer cannot be the primary detector for consultation windows — the BQK site and the Prime Minister's concept-document repository must be.

description: Serbian-language searching found KoSSev but did not surface Kosovo Online, Radio KIM or RTK2 with any banking-regulation content in this pass.

result.result_summary: Only one Serbian-language Kosovo outlet (KoSSev) confirmed with on-topic banking-supervision material.

why_it_matters: The Serb-bank licensing dispute is a major supervisory story with a single confirmed local-language channel; single-source risk.

description: Two domains appeared for Insajderi (insajderi.com and insajderi.org) and two for Koha's economy section (www.koha.net and apps.koha.net), and two for the Assembly (kuvendikosoves.org, assemblyofkosovo.org).

result.result_summary: Canonical hosts not determined; both variants recorded rather than guessed.

why_it_matters: A crawler pointed at the non-canonical host may silently collect nothing or duplicate content.

description: Direct WebFetch of https://bqk-kos.org/?lang=sr returned HTTP 403 Forbidden, so the Serbian-language section structure of the CBK site could not be enumerated in this pass.

result.result_summary: 403 on the regulator's own Serbian-language landing page; the site is clearly live (search engines index SRB-*.pdf regulation files under /wp-content/uploads/2025/12/), so this reads as bot defence, not a dead host. Recorded as unverified, not dead.

why_it_matters: The single most important source in this cell cannot be collected with a naive fetcher; the collection pipeline needs a browser-like agent or an allowlisted crawler, otherwise the entire Serbian-language regulatory feed silently returns nothing.

description: No dedicated Serbian-language public-consultation portal or consultation register for CBK draft regulations was located.

result.result_summary: Searches in Serbian for CBK consultation terms surfaced only news coverage of finished decisions, not a konsultacije/javna rasprava page in Serbian. Kosovo's central government consultation platform (konsultimet.rks-gov.net) was not confirmed to carry CBK items or Serbian translations in this pass.

why_it_matters: If draft CBK rules are consulted only in Albanian, Serbian-language monitoring will always be reactive — catching rules after adoption rather than during the comment window, which is precisely the deadline intelligence this workstream needs.

description: The Office of the Language Commissioner's canonical domain was not confirmed by a successful fetch.

result.result_summary: The institution and its 2024 complaint statistics were confirmed through KoSSev and UNS reporting, but its own website URL (zkgjnj.rks-gov.net) is inferred from the rks-gov.net naming convention and must be resolved by the verification pass.

why_it_matters: This source is the structural indicator of Serbian-language publication compliance; an unresolved URL means the pipeline would fall back on second-hand media reporting only.

description: No Ombudsperson Institution (OIK) report or ex-officio case specifically on the Regulation on Cash Operations was found in Serbian.

result.result_summary: Search combining Ombudsman, Serbian-language report and cash-operations regulation terms returned only generic institutional pages; no matching document surfaced.

why_it_matters: An OIK opinion would be the most authoritative non-partisan assessment of the regulation's effect on Serb-majority municipalities; its apparent absence (or non-indexing) means this angle is currently covered only by advocacy sources on both sides.

description: No consistent Serbian-language terminology was found for CBK supervisory/enforcement actions against unlicensed payment providers.

result.result_summary: Enforcement in Serb-majority areas is reported in police/political vocabulary ('zatvorene filijale', 'zaplenjeno', 'nelegalna finansijska institucija') rather than supervisory vocabulary ('oduzimanje licence', 'nadzorna mera', 'sankcija'), so keyword lists built from supervisory terms will miss most events.

why_it_matters: Keyword design for this cell must use police/political Serbian vocabulary alongside regulatory vocabulary, or enforcement events will be systematically under-collected.

description: Serbian-language searching using the correct statutory phrasing (obavestenje klijentima, izmena opstih uslova poslovanja) returned almost exclusively Serbian and Montenegrin domestic banks (Addiko, OTP, Halkbank, Raiffeisen RS, Komercijalna, Banca Intesa, CKB), not Kosovo-licensed banks. No Kosovo bank was found publishing a structured Serbian-language customer-notice feed.

result.result_summary: The only Serbian-language artefacts located on a Kosovo bank domain were ProCredit's .sr e-banking manuals. NLB Kosovo, Raiffeisen Kosovo, TEB, BKT, BPB and Banka Ekonomike surfaced only sq and en surfaces in this pass.

why_it_matters: If regulatory change reaches Serbian-speaking customers in Kosovo at all, it may do so through branch notices or Serbia-facing media rather than the web, creating a monitoring blind spot for northern-municipality payment and account-migration effects. It also risks a collector mistaking Serbian-domiciled bank results for Kosovo ones.

description: Searches for standalone compliance / AML / FATCA disclosure pages on the individual Kosovo bank websites (in sq using 'pajtueshmeria' and in en) did not surface dedicated per-bank compliance landing pages.

result.result_summary: Compliance visibility in Kosovo appears to sit at the Kosovo Banking Association committee level rather than on individual bank sites; the banks' compliance content is embedded inside T&C and annual-report documents instead.

why_it_matters: The cell's 'compliance pages' sub-hypothesis is weaker than expected. Collection effort should be reallocated from per-bank compliance pages to T&C version diffs, tariff PDFs and parent-group Pillar 3 disclosures, which is where the regulatory signal actually lives.

description: Searches in sq for 2025/2026 SEPA and IBAN migration notices addressed to customers returned CBK/press-level coverage (pre-application completed, process suspended pending constitutional review of three laws) but no bank-issued customer migration notice.

result.result_summary: The only bank-level IBAN notices found (BPB, NLB converter) relate to the earlier domestic IBAN/XK05 numbering regulation, not to SEPA accession.

why_it_matters: Confirms SEPA has not yet reached the customer-notice stage in Kosovo. The first bank-issued SEPA customer notice will therefore be a genuinely high-value early signal that accession has moved from legal-harmonisation to operational implementation, and monitoring should be primed to catch it.

description: Two target pages did not fetch cleanly: ProCredit's news index returned HTTP 500, and TEB's njoftim-per-klientet permalink resolved to the site homepage rather than the article.

result.result_summary: Both are recorded as unverified hypotheses, not dead sources — their content was visible in search-engine indexes, indicating live-but-defended or moved-permalink conditions.

why_it_matters: A naive liveness checker would wrongly drop two of the most important notice feeds in the cell. The verification pass should retry with browser-grade fetching and treat 500/soft-redirect as retryable.

description: No Kosovo bank was found to maintain a dated archive of superseded customer notices or previous terms versions as a browsable list.

result.result_summary: Historical reconstruction depends on incidental URL conventions (BKT /content/YYYY/MM/, TEB Cmimorja_DD.MM.YYYY.pdf, BPB wp-content/uploads/YYYY/MM/) rather than any publisher-provided archive.

why_it_matters: Backfill of the regulatory timeline before the monitoring start date will be partial and must lean on web-archive snapshots; forward-looking snapshotting must start immediately or the history is unrecoverable.

description: No dedicated Kosovo-based fintech or payments regulatory conference with a published agenda was found for 2026. The closest is the regional Balkan Payment Forum in Tirana and the Kosovo Banking Association's own Payments Forum.

result.result_summary: Searches on Kosovo fintech/payments conference agendas returned only regional and global event calendars plus the association's Payments Forum 2025 page.

why_it_matters: Payment-rule weak signals for Kosovo have to be picked up from the banking association's events and from regional forums where Kosovo speakers appear, rather than from a domestic fintech conference circuit that does not appear to exist.

description: bankassoc-kos.com (Kosovo Banking Association), the highest-value source in this cell, returned HTTP 403 Forbidden on every direct fetch attempt (both https://bankassoc-kos.com/events/ and https://www.bankassoc-kos.com/Al/trajnimet/), while its pages are indexed and serving content to search crawlers.

result.result_summary: Two fetch attempts, two 403s. Content confirmed live and current via the search index (events dated into October 2026).

why_it_matters: Hypothesis: bot protection / UA filtering, not a dead site. The collector for this source must be browser-based rather than a plain HTTP client, otherwise the single most productive weak-signal channel in the cell will be silently empty. Do not mark this domain dead.

description: No GIZ Kosovo project specifically targeting banking regulation or financial-sector supervision was located. The only GIZ Kosovo financial project found ('Improving financial governance in Kosovo') addresses public financial management, not bank supervision.

result.result_summary: Both an Albanian-language and an English-language donor search returned only the good-financial-governance project; GIZ appears in Kosovo mainly on energy and ICT.

why_it_matters: The seed query's assumption that GIZ is a live actor in Kosovo financial-sector regulation is not supported by what was found. IFC/SECO, the World Bank, the EU/ESCB consortium and the IMF are the actors actually visible in this space, and collection effort should be weighted accordingly.

description: No current USAID Kosovo project page on financial-sector regulation was found. The only USAID reference surfaced was historical — international banking supervision consultants funded by USAID helping establish Kosovo's banking supervision function, cited in an early BQK/BPK annual report.

result.result_summary: USAID appears only as a historical actor and as a general ICT-sector donor; no live project page for financial regulation was retrieved.

why_it_matters: Given the state of US development funding, USAID should be treated as a low-priority or dormant channel for this cell unless a live project page is later confirmed. Recording it as an assumed active donor would be a fabrication.

description: Serbian-language (sr) searching returned no Kosovo-specific event, training or donor artefact. The one Cyrillic-script hit relevant to Kosovo was a Macedonian-language report of the regional ESCB/IPA programme in which Kosovo's central bank is a beneficiary, plus a Republika Srpska banking-agency page on the same programme.

result.result_summary: One sr/Cyrillic query executed; results skewed to North Macedonia, Serbia and BiH institutions rather than Kosovo bodies.

why_it_matters: For this cell, Serbian-language material about Kosovo financial regulation appears to be produced mainly by non-Kosovo institutions covering shared regional programmes. Serbian-language collection should target regional/peer institutions and Serbian-language Kosovo outlets, not BQK itself, whose sr output was not observed in this run. sr coverage of this cell is genuinely thin and should be flagged as such rather than assumed.

description: The session's web-search budget (200 calls) was exhausted before two planned lines of enquiry could be run: World Bank FinSAC / Vienna Initiative workshop agendas involving Kosovo, and AMIK (Asociacioni i Institucioneve Mikrofinanciare të Kosovës) training and conference activity.

result.result_summary: Two queries were issued and refused by the search budget guard; no results obtained.

why_it_matters: These are plausible additional weak-signal channels for this cell (FinSAC runs supervisory workshops for SEE authorities; AMIK is the non-bank counterpart to the Banking Association and would carry MFI-regulation signals). They remain unexamined, not absent.

description: The CEF (Center of Excellence in Finance, Ljubljana) training-calendar URL could not be confirmed. Only the institution's homepage, an archived about-us page and its team page were surfaced, together with confirmation that Kosovo is one of its member constituencies.

result.result_summary: Searches confirmed the institution and Kosovo membership but returned no calendar/learning-programme URL.

why_it_matters: The source is recorded with reduced confidence and its collection method explicitly starts with locating the calendar path. It must not be treated as a confirmed feed.

description: Searched in Albanian for a CBK/BQK public-consultation page for draft regulations ('projektrregullore', 'konsultim publik', 'afati i komenteve') and for CBK entries on the central konsultimet.rks-gov.net platform.

result.result_summary: No CBK-run consultation register and no CBK consultation on the central platform surfaced. Results returned only finalised CBK regulation PDFs, plus consultation notices from unrelated bodies (Prosecutorial Council, Judicial Council). The central platform's institution filter is oriented to ministries and the PM Office; the CBK is an independent institution and appears not to consult through it.

why_it_matters: If CBK secondary rules (rregullore) are not consulted on any indexed platform, deadline intelligence for the supervisor's own rulebook cannot come from a consultation feed — it must come from diffing the CBK rulebook index and from Wayback snapshots. That materially changes the collection design for A3.

description: Serbian-language search for a commercial consolidated-law database covering Kosovo acts ('propisi', 'baza propisa', 'zakon o platnim uslugama').

result.result_summary: All commercial consolidated-law vendors returned (paragraf.rs, cekos.rs, porezionline.rs) cover Republic of Serbia legislation, not Kosovo acts. No Kosovo equivalent of a paid consolidation service was found.

why_it_matters: There is no commercial fallback if GZK consolidation lags. Kosovo version history is single-sourced on gzk.rks-gov.net plus web archives, which raises the value of our own snapshotting and makes GZK a single point of failure worth monitoring for availability.

description: The cell brief names the consultation platform 'e-Konsultimet'.

result.result_summary: The actual platform is 'Platforma e Konsultimeve Publike' at konsultimet.rks-gov.net (no 'e-' prefix, no hyphen). Verified by fetching about.php and consultationsList.php.

why_it_matters: Collectors keyed on an 'e-konsultimet' hostname would silently fetch nothing. Recording the correct host prevents a false-negative feed.

description: Fetched https://konsultimet.rks-gov.net/consultationsList.php to enumerate open consultations and deadlines.

result.result_summary: The page returned the filter interface (institution dropdown, open/closed status, date range, name search) but no populated result rows — results appear to load via a POST/AJAX step rather than in the initial GET.

why_it_matters: A naive GET-and-parse collector will report zero consultations and look 'green' while collecting nothing. The collector must replicate the form POST or drive a headless browser.

description: Attempted plain fetch of the CBK legal-framework index https://bqk-kos.org/?id=121.

result.result_summary: HTTP 403 Forbidden. PDF paths on the same host are indexed by search engines and served. Hypothesis: WAF/user-agent filtering, site live. Recorded as unverified, NOT dead.

why_it_matters: The primary rulebook index for the supervisor needs a browser-grade fetcher; otherwise the whole CBK leg of A3 silently fails.

description: Planned further Serbian-language queries (PKIE / Nacionalni program, 'konsolidovani tekst zakona Kosovo', Wayback CDX coverage for gzk.rks-gov.net) and an Albanian query on the Ministry of Finance consultation subpage.

result.result_summary: The session web-search budget (200/200) was exhausted before these ran. No results obtained; these are untested leads, not dead ends.

why_it_matters: Serbian-language coverage of this cell rests on one executed sr query, so sr-side aggregators may be under-represented in this slice.

description: No standalone CBK public register page for payment institutions, electronic money institutions and registered AISPs was located, despite Regulation B15 and Art. 18 of the Law on Payment System obliging CBK to maintain and publish one. Searched in Albanian ('regjistri publik i institucioneve të pagesave dhe parasë elektronike') and English.

result.result_summary: Only the legal obligation and the consolidated all-sector register PDF were found; no dedicated PI/EMI/AISP register URL surfaced in search results.

why_it_matters: Payments is the core commercial interest of this run. Without the PI/EMI/AISP register the fintech/PSP population cannot be enumerated from the regulator side, and the consolidated PDF may not break these classes out.

description: No dedicated CBK enforcement/sanctions bulletin or public list of imposed administrative-punitive measures per institution was found. Enforcement appears only as aggregate counts inside the annual report (e.g. 'in seven cases administrative-punitive measures were adopted' for 2020).

result.result_summary: Searched sq ('masat ndëshkuese', 'shqiptimi i gjobave', 'njoftim vendim') and en ('CBK Kosovo enforcement measures sanctions'); no per-case notice page or register of sanctions surfaced.

why_it_matters: Enforcement notices are the observable proof of which rules bite. If CBK genuinely does not publish per-case sanctions, enforcement intelligence for Kosovo must be reconstructed from annual reports, court reporting and media — a much weaker and lagging signal.

description: No separate 'annual supervision report' (a supervision-only annual publication, as e.g. Bank of Albania issues 'Raportet Vjetore të Mbikëqyrjes Bankare') was found for CBK Kosovo. Supervision appears as a chapter of the general Annual Report and via the Financial Stability Report.

result.result_summary: Albanian-language searches for 'raporti vjetor i mbikëqyrjes financiare BQK' returned the Bank of Albania equivalent, not a Kosovo one.

why_it_matters: The collector should not wait for an artefact that likely does not exist; supervision monitoring must instead target the Annual Report chapter, the Financial Stability Report and the monthly financial-system information report.

description: bqk-kos.org (and the env2.bqk-kos.org mirror) returned HTTP 403 Forbidden to both WebFetch and curl with a realistic desktop browser User-Agent, on HTML pages. PDF assets under /wp-content/uploads/ were reachable in search indexing.

result.result_summary: Two independent fetch methods 403'd on the register hub page; the site is clearly live and indexed, so this is bot protection, not a dead site. Recorded as unverified, not dead.

why_it_matters: Any production collector for this cell must budget for a headless browser / anti-bot-aware fetcher for CBK HTML pages; a naive HTTP client will produce false 'source dead' signals across the most important domain in the cell.

description: Serbian-language (sr) coverage of CBK registers is very thin. The only confirmed sr artefacts are the ?lang=sr annual report PDFs (Godišnji Izveštaj). No Serbian-language version of the licensed-institution register list, licensing pages or enforcement material was located.

result.result_summary: Query 'Centralna banka Kosova spisak licenciranih banaka mikrofinansijskih institucija registar' returned Wikipedia and CBK annual-report PDFs only.

why_it_matters: If sr is a required monitoring language, the register layer may simply not exist in Serbian, meaning sr coverage for XK must be sourced from the annual reports plus Serbian-language Kosovo media rather than from the regulator's register pages.

description: No CBK public-consultation portal or 'draft regulations open for comment' page was located in this pass, in either sq or en.

result.result_summary: Regulation PDFs were found in final form under /korniza-ligjore/rregulloret/ and /wp-content/uploads/, but no consultation index, comment deadline listing, or draft-regulation section surfaced.

why_it_matters: 'Consultations' and 'deadlines' are explicit run topics; if CBK consults only by direct letter to licensed institutions, forward-looking regulatory intelligence for Kosovo must come from the newsroom and from the industry association rather than a consultation register.

description: Direct WebFetch of the Assembly's own pages returned HTTP 403 Forbidden on two independent paths: https://www.kuvendikosoves.org/shq/projektligjet-dhe-ligjet/ and https://kuvendikosoves.org/shq/projektligjet/projektligji/?draftlaw=266.

result.result_summary: 403 on both attempts; the same URLs are indexed and summarised by search engines, so the host is almost certainly live and bot-defended rather than dead. Recorded as unverified, not dead.

why_it_matters: The Assembly register is the upstream half of this coverage cell. Any collection design must assume a browser-like client (headless browser or realistic UA/headers), and should keep the assembly-kosova.org / assemblyofkosovo.org mirrors as fallbacks.

description: No structured per-bill stage record (first reading date, second reading date, committee report link) could be confirmed for the banking law 08/L-304 or the Draft Law on Payment Services from search results alone.

result.result_summary: Searches in sq and en for the 08/L-304 committee amendment report and for a first-reading record of the payment services bill returned no matching Assembly document.

why_it_matters: The reading-stage timeline — the core of the 'when will the deadline clock start' question — is likely only visible inside the 403-blocked per-bill pages, so stage tracking depends entirely on solving the fetch blocker.

description: No RSS/Atom feed, open API, or bulk-download endpoint was identified for either the Official Gazette (gzk.rks-gov.net) or the Assembly bill register.

result.result_summary: The GZK portal exposes advanced search, by-year browsing, a subscription option and mobile apps, but no documented machine interface was found; the Assembly site likewise showed none in search results.

why_it_matters: Ingestion will be scraping-based and therefore fragile to CMS redesigns. The GZK mobile apps are the most promising lead for an undocumented JSON backend and should be investigated before committing to HTML parsing.

description: For the new Law No. 08/L-304 on Banks (Gazette Nr. 2 / 27 January 2026), only the CBK-hosted gazetted PDF (sq and sr) was located; the corresponding gzk.rks-gov.net ActDocumentDetail record was not identified in searches.

result.result_summary: CBK copies carry the full gazette header, but the canonical GZK ActID for this act remains unknown.

why_it_matters: For a compliance-deadline product, the canonical gazette record should be the citation of record. An ActID resolution step (GZK search by title/number) is a required part of collection design.

description: Serbian-language coverage of the parliamentary stage (as opposed to the final gazetted text) is thin.

result.result_summary: Serbian searches surfaced the sr register and session pages plus sr gazetted statute PDFs, but no sr-language committee amendment reports or sr per-bill stage pages for banking/payments bills.

why_it_matters: sr is a mandatory language for this run and an official language of Kosovo. If sr-language bill-stage documents genuinely do not exist, that is a structural property of the source landscape that downstream analysis must record rather than treat as a collection failure.

description: Searched specifically for a MONEYVAL mutual evaluation report (MER) for Kosovo and for Kosovo's MONEYVAL membership status.

result.result_summary: No MONEYVAL MER for Kosovo was found and Kosovo does not appear among MONEYVAL's members/jurisdictions subject to its evaluation procedures. Kosovo's AML/CFT compliance is instead assessed through the Council of Europe / EU joint 'Project against Economic Crime in Kosovo' (PECK, and PECK II), whose assessment, monitoring and follow-up reports are hosted on rm.coe.int and apply MONEYVAL-style methodology.

why_it_matters: The cell brief assumes a MONEYVAL evaluation of Kosovo whose action-plan dates become national deadlines. That mechanism exists, but the publisher and document series are PECK/PECK II (plus the annual EU enlargement report), not MONEYVAL plenary follow-up. Monitoring the MONEYVAL evaluations page alone would produce a permanent false negative for Kosovo.

description: Searched in Albanian and English for a published, citable statement of Kosovo's AML reporting thresholds and filing deadlines (STR/SAR turnaround, cash-transaction reporting threshold, cross-border currency declaration).

result.result_summary: No page stating concrete thresholds or filing clocks was surfaced. The FIU report-online page does not list report types, thresholds or deadlines; it defers to the legislation section. The values presumably sit inside Law 05/L-096 and the individual udhëzime administrative PDFs, which were not opened in this pass.

why_it_matters: Deadline logic is the core value of this cell. The deadlines are not on any index page and must be extracted from PDF full text, so collection design must include PDF text extraction, not just link monitoring.

description: Searched (sq/en) for a published Kosovo National Risk Assessment (Vlerësimi Kombëtar i Rrezikut) for money laundering and terrorist financing.

result.result_summary: The FIU legislation index lists a 'risk assessment reports' category, but no NRA document or dedicated NRA landing page was located in this pass. Search results surfaced only the older PECK assessment material and generic institution-level risk-assessment commentary.

why_it_matters: The NRA drives the risk-based obligations imposed on banks (sectoral risk ratings, EDD triggers). Its absence from search results may mean it is unpublished, published only as an internal document, or buried in an FIU PDF listing — each implies a different collection strategy.

description: Serbian-language (sr) searching for the Kosovo FIU produced almost no Kosovo-institution results.

result.result_summary: The query 'Jedinica za finansijsku obaveštajnu Kosovo sprečavanje pranja novca izveštavanje banke uputstvo' returned mostly Serbia's own APML/NBS and Republic-of-Serbia material, plus CBK regulation PDFs served under the ?lang=sr / /srpski/ paths. The correct Serbian acronym for the Kosovo body appears to be FOJ-K (Finansijska obaveštajna jedinica), but no sr-language FIU landing page was directly confirmed.

why_it_matters: Serbian is an official language in Kosovo and the FIU site advertises a Serbian version, but generic sr queries are heavily polluted by Serbia-proper AML authorities. sr collection must be domain-scoped (site:fiu.rks-gov.net, site:bqk-kos.org, ?lang=sr paths) rather than keyword-driven, or it will silently collect the wrong jurisdiction.

description: The Albanian phrase 'masat kufizuese ndaj Kosovës' is dangerously polysemous.

result.result_summary: Searching for Kosovo financial sanctions returns two unrelated things: (a) Kosovo's own regime for implementing UN/EU financial sanctions against designated persons (Law 08/L-146, Law 03/L-183), and (b) the EU's political restrictive measures imposed ON Kosovo after the 2023 northern-Kosovo tensions. Kallxo coverage of the latter dominated the results.

why_it_matters: A naive keyword collector on 'masat kufizuese' + 'Kosovë' will mostly harvest EU-Kosovo political news, not the compliance obligations banks must screen against. Queries need disambiguating anchors such as 'lista e sanksioneve', 'personat e shpallur', 'ngrirje e aseteve', or the law numbers.

description: Direct text of Law 08/L-146 on international financial sanctions was not retrieved.

result.result_summary: The law is listed on the FIU legislation index, but neither its gazette page nor its PDF was opened in this pass; sq searching on the law number returned adjacent material only. No conclusion about availability should be drawn — this is unverified, not missing.

why_it_matters: Law 08/L-146 is the legal hook for national designations and asset-freeze timelines, which is where sanctions deadlines for banks originate. It should be resolved to a gazette ActID in the next pass.

description: Could not locate a canonical, directly-linkable ATK register page listing currently licensed/certified fiscal-device suppliers and certified device models.

result.result_summary: Press reporting names four historically licensed PEF suppliers (Gekos, Dukagjini, Enternet, Service Global) and states the list is published on the ATK website, but no direct URL for that register surfaced in sq or en searches; the ATK site also failed automated fetch on a TLS chain error.

why_it_matters: The certified-supplier register is the single most decision-relevant artefact for a payments-hardware business entering or partnering in Kosovo; without a stable URL, monitoring must fall back on press and the SEF application portal.

description: Serbian-language ('sr') searching returned almost no Kosovo-specific fiscal-device regulatory material; results were dominated by Republic of Serbia sources (purs.gov.rs, paragraf.rs, aktivasistem.com).

result.result_summary: The query 'poreska administracija Kosova fiskalne kase pravilnik uputstvo' surfaced only one genuinely Kosovo item — ATK's Serbian-language tax legislation compendium PDF — with the rest being Serbian national fiscalization rules that are out of scope and actively confusing.

why_it_matters: 'fiskalne kase' and 'pravilnik' are high-noise terms for Kosovo: they retrieve Serbia's separate fiscalization regime. Any sr-language monitoring for this cell must be domain-scoped (atk-ks.org, gzk.rks-gov.net, dogana.rks-gov.net) rather than keyword-only.

description: Automated fetch of the primary ATK website failed on TLS certificate chain verification; the MFPT homepage returned an effectively empty document.

result.result_summary: https://www.atk-ks.org/ and https://www.atk-ks.org/njoftime/ both returned 'unable to verify the first certificate'; https://mf.rks-gov.net/ returned only a site title with no navigation.

why_it_matters: Both are hypotheses about collection mechanics, not liveness verdicts — the sites are clearly live given indexed content and working PDF links. The collection layer will need relaxed TLS chain handling and headless rendering for these two domains.

description: No dedicated Kosovo e-invoicing (B2B/B2G electronic invoicing) portal or standalone mandate page was found distinct from the fiscalization framework.

result.result_summary: E-invoice obligations appear embedded within the fiscal-device instructions (e.g. UA Nr. 02/2018 covering electronic invoices for internet supplies) and within the emerging SEF architecture, rather than as a separate e-invoicing programme with its own portal.

why_it_matters: Monitoring should therefore treat 'e-faturimi' as a subtopic of the fiscalization instruments rather than expecting a separate rule-making stream; a separate portal may appear later as SEF matures.

description: Several natural-language queries leak heavily into Albania (AL) rather than Kosovo (XK) sources.

result.result_summary: 'Ministria e Financave' and 'arkat fiskale' returned financa.gov.al, shqiptarja.com, ligjetebiznesit.al and alprofitconsult.al — Albania's separate fiscalization regime and ministry.

why_it_matters: Kosovo queries must be pinned with 'Kosovë', 'ATK', 'MFPT', 'rks-gov.net' or domain filters, otherwise Albanian fiscalization deadlines will be mistaken for Kosovar ones — a material risk given both countries run Albanian-language fiscalization programmes.

description: No Kosovo Competition Authority decision, sector inquiry or commitment specifically on interbank/interchange fees (komisionet ndërbankare) was found in sq or en searches.

result.result_summary: Searches surfaced only Albanian (AL) Competition Authority decisions on banks (e.g. Vendimi 174) and generic AKK pages; the specific interchange topic returned nothing for Kosovo. Kosovar media report an AKK preliminary investigation into banks with no published decision yet.

why_it_matters: Interchange caps in Kosovo may still originate from the central bank rather than the competition authority; the cell must not assume an AKK interchange file exists until a decision register is actually reachable.

description: https://ak.rks-gov.net/ did not resolve (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND) from this environment.

result.result_summary: One failed DNS resolution against the domain that search engines consistently list as the AKK official site. Not confirmed dead; likely a network/DNS or geo restriction on this host.

why_it_matters: The competition regulator is the highest-value node in this cell; a false 'dead source' verdict would silently drop interchange and bank-merger coverage. Must be retried by the deterministic verification pass from a different network.

description: No public register of qualified trust-service providers (ofrues të shërbimeve të besuara / qualified e-signature certificate issuers) for Kosovo was located at a stable official URL.

result.result_summary: Sources describe an eIDAS-aligned law supervised by the ministry responsible for information technology together with the information agency, and state that certified providers exist, but no official trusted list URL was found in sq or en searches.

why_it_matters: Remote onboarding and e-contracting by banks depend on which providers are qualified; without a trusted-list source, e-signature compliance changes cannot be tracked at the provider level.

description: Serbian-language (sr) versions of the primary regulator sites in this cell were not located.

result.result_summary: AIP is officially bilingual by name (Agencija za Informacije i Privatnost) and FSDK publishes at least one sr leaflet, but no sr-language decision or consultation sections were found on aip.rks-gov.net, fsdk.org, arkep-rks.org or konsumatori.rks-gov.net. sr coverage currently rests on media (KosovaPress /srb/) and the official gazette.

why_it_matters: The run mandates sr coverage; if sr content genuinely does not exist on these sites, collection must rely on gzk.rks-gov.net sr act texts plus sr media, and this limitation must be recorded rather than treated as a search failure.

description: The consumer-protection portal konsumatori.rks-gov.net was reported by Kosovar economic media (Aug 2026) as the target of a cyber attack.

result.result_summary: Reported outage/compromise; the site was not fetched in this run, so its current state is unverified.

why_it_matters: The main consumer-protection publication channel for bank fee/disclosure enforcement may be intermittently unavailable; collection should include a fallback via mint.rks-gov.net and the official gazette.

description: No public, per-meeting agenda, minutes or 'jointly agreed follow-up actions' document for the EU–Kosovo SAA Sub-committee on Economic and Financial Issues and Statistics could be located; only EEAS press releases summarising each meeting were found.

result.result_summary: Searches surfaced press releases for the 5th, 6th and 7th sub-committee meetings but no underlying documents, no document register, and no fixed meeting calendar.

why_it_matters: The follow-up action lists are the crispest EU-driven deadline artefact for Kosovo financial-sector rules; without them the pipeline must be reconstructed from press releases plus the next annual country report, losing several months of lead time.

description: No Kosovo-specific EU document was found that explicitly names DORA, MiCA or PSR as instruments Kosovo is scheduled to transpose.

result.result_summary: Targeted searches combining Kosovo with DORA / MiCA / PSD2 / PSR / AMLR against IPA and enlargement domains returned only generic IPA III financing announcements and no instrument-level commitment.

why_it_matters: It is a real possibility that Kosovo's EU-driven pipeline is currently anchored on older instruments (PSD2/AMLD, banking recovery and resolution) rather than the 2023–2025 acquis wave. Treating DORA/MiCA transposition as scheduled would be an unsupported assumption; this must be confirmed by reading the country-report chapters directly rather than inferred.

description: No Serbian-language (sr) Kosovo-government source for the EU-driven rule pipeline was located in this pass.

result.result_summary: Serbian-language searching returned EU/EEAS and Serbia-focused material plus the CBK Serbian annual report, but no sr-language version of PKIE/PKZMSA or an sr Assembly EU-integration page was confirmed.

why_it_matters: Kosovo is officially bilingual; an sr-language gap risks missing documents published only on the Serbian-language mirrors of rks-gov.net sites, and weakens coverage of the Serb-majority banking constituency.

description: Commission enlargement document URLs are opaque, UUID-based download links with a filename query parameter rather than stable permalinks.

result.result_summary: Two different UUID URLs were observed for the 2025 Kosovo Report; the 2024 report uses a third. No stable canonical URL pattern was identified.

why_it_matters: Any stored URL for a Commission country report is likely to break between cycles, so collection must resolve documents from the enlargement package landing page each year rather than by stored link, with ecoi.net as a fallback resolver.

description: A Serbian-language search using Cyrillic IFI terminology ('ММФ извештај Косово банкарски сектор супервизија препоруке') returned no Kosovo-specific IFI material; results were dominated by North Macedonia and generic supervision pages.

result.result_summary: Zero usable Serbian-language sources for IFI reporting on Kosovo were found in this run. IFIs publish on Kosovo in English only; Serbian-language secondary coverage appears to originate from Serbia-based outlets that were not surfaced by this query.

why_it_matters: The run requires sr coverage. If no sr-language IFI channel exists, sr coverage for this cell must come from Serbian-language media in Kosovo/Serbia, which needs a separate targeted query set (Latin-script Serbian, e.g. 'MMF izveštaj Kosovo bankarski sektor').

description: No Albanian- or Serbian-language versions of IMF, World Bank, EBRD, EIB or CEB reports on Kosovo were located; all primary IFI documents found are English-only.

result.result_summary: Local-language access to this cell is indirect only — via CBK press releases (sq) and Albanian economic press summarising the English originals.

why_it_matters: Any sq/sr monitoring for this cell must be built on national-counterpart and press proxies rather than on IFI sites themselves; collection design should not expect language toggles on IFI domains.

description: Direct fetch of the IMF Kosovo country page (https://www.imf.org/en/Countries/UVK) returned HTTP 403 Forbidden.

result.result_summary: Treated as a bot-defence hypothesis, not a dead URL — IMF Kosovo content is clearly live and reachable via search results and direct PDF links on imf.org and elibrary.imf.org.

why_it_matters: The collection layer for imf.org needs a browser-grade fetcher or the elibrary/media PDF paths, otherwise the highest-priority source in this cell silently yields nothing.

description: The World Bank Projects & Operations list for Kosovo renders client-side; a static fetch returned only the page shell.

result.result_summary: No project rows retrievable without JS execution; the World Bank Projects API is the correct access path.

why_it_matters: Prevents a naive HTML scraper from being scheduled against a source that would appear live but always return empty.

description: No full joint IMF-World Bank FSAP (Financial Sector Assessment Program) for Kosovo was found; the equivalent function is served by the IMF Financial Sector Stability Review (2019) and its 2025/2026 follow-up.

result.result_summary: Searches for a Kosovo FSAP surfaced only FSSR and TA reports.

why_it_matters: Analysts should not wait for or search on 'FSAP' for Kosovo — FSSR is the correct document family and the correct search key.

description: Despite targeted Albanian-language searching ('Shoqata e Bankave të Kosovës reagon draft rregullore BQK konsultim publik komente'), no dedicated page or archive of SHBK formal comment letters on CBK draft regulations was surfaced. Search results for that query returned only CBK's own regulation PDFs.

result.result_summary: SHBK regulatory engagement appears to be documented indirectly (committee mandate text, joint workshops, magazine articles) rather than as a published consultation-response library.

why_it_matters: The most decision-relevant artefact for this cell — a comment letter naming contested articles and requested deadline extensions — may only exist inside CBK consultation files or member-only areas, so collection must lean on konsultimet.rks-gov.net, CBK consultation pages, and media coverage instead.

description: Both peak sector associations — bankassoc-kos.com and amik.org — returned HTTP 403 Forbidden to plain fetches, while their sub-pages are indexed and served in search results.

result.result_summary: Two 403s recorded; treated as bot defence, not as dead sites.

why_it_matters: Automated collection of the two highest-value sources in this cell will need browser-emulating fetchers; a naive crawler would wrongly mark them offline.

description: Serbian-language searching for a Kosovo banking or microfinance association ('Udruženje banaka Kosova', 'udruženje poslodavaca', 'propisi') found no sr-language banking-industry association for Kosovo. Only a general Serbian-language chamber structure (Privredna komora Kosova i Metohije) and Serbia-side chambers surfaced.

result.result_summary: No sr-language equivalent of SHBK/AMIK exists as far as searching could establish.

why_it_matters: sr-language coverage of industry self-organisation in this cell is structurally thin; sr-language signal on financial regulation must be sourced from minority media (KoSSev, Kosovo Online, RFE/Slobodna Evropa) and the CBK's own sr-language regulation pages rather than from an association.

description: The AmCham Kosovo site listed committees including Defense & Security and Life Sciences & Healthcare; no dedicated banking or financial-services committee was visible on the fetched page, although banks (BKT, NLB Banka, TEB) are patron members and AmCham sits on Finance/Tax/Customs consultative councils.

result.result_summary: Financial-services advocacy at AmCham appears to run through general fiscal/economic councils, not a named banking committee.

why_it_matters: Collection should target AmCham's tax and economic-policy output rather than searching for a banking committee that may not exist.

description: Searching for Aleanca Kosovare e Bizneseve returned only a regional-office site (akb-gjakove.com) plus heavy media coverage; the national AKB web domain was not established within this run.

result.result_summary: AKB is trackable via media but its authoritative own-site channel is unconfirmed.

why_it_matters: Without the national domain, AKB positions can only be collected second-hand, losing the full text of any statement.
